subject: Enclave observability export policy & trace hooks (NovaBank)
messages:
From: Amal Singh <amal.singh@novabank.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Observability exports for NovaBank enclave - clarifications

Hi Ethan,

Thanks for taking this on. We're prepping our SOC review and need details on how Redwood will export logs/metrics/traces from the private enclave. High-level questions: 

- Can the exporter ship directly to our Splunk HEC over mutual TLS, or do you require a forwarder in our VPC?
- What are the egress allowlist IPs/ports and can they be pinned to a regional range?
- How do you handle sensitive fields — any built-in PII scrubbing or does that live in our forwarder?
- Trace hooks: what span attributes are emitted by default and can we add stable correlation headers (x-nb-trace-id)?
- For evidence requested by auditors, can you provide a signed bundle (logs + trace samples + manifest) on an SFTP endpoint?

We have a short window for our SOC snapshot (target week of Nov 29). Can you confirm the recommended architecture and an evidence delivery plan?

Thanks,
Amal
Security Engineering — NovaBank

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
To: Amal Singh <amal.singh@novabank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-13T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability exports for NovaBank enclave - clarifications

Hi Amal — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then I'll loop in Kim and Marissa for the deep-dive artifacts: 

- Splunk HEC: Supported over mutual TLS from our enclave forwarder. We can also support a customer-managed forwarder in your VPC that pushes to HEC if you prefer no direct egress from Redwood pods.
- Egress allowlist: we publish regional ranges; for NovaBank we can provide a narrow set of egress IPs + FQDNs and a port matrix (HEC: 443).
- PII scrubbing: Redwood runtime supports field-level redaction rules at the forwarder; however most customers enforce an upstream filter in their forwarder for policy reasons.
- Tracing: default spans include request-id, model, route, token-counts; we can add a stable header (x-nb-trace-id) for cross-system correlation.
- Evidence bundle: yes — can produce a signed tarball with manifest and checksum; we can deliver via SFTP or a signed Drive link.

I've attached a short export policy draft and will ask Kim to attach the tracehook YAML and notes on Splunk mTLS. Proposal: internal handshake doc + one-week canary to validate HEC ingestion and retention mapping before the SOC snapshot.

Attaching: redwood-enclave-export-policy-v1.pdf (policy diff)

Best,
Ethan Park
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Observability exports for NovaBank enclave - clarifications

Ethan — adding specifics for the SOC thread. Attachments: tracehook-spec.yaml (span attributes + example), splunk-hec-mtls-notes.md (operational checklist).

Key tech answers: 
1) Direct HEC over mTLS: supported. Our forwarder initiates TLS with client cert auth; we rotate certs on a 90-day cadence unless customer supplies pinning/rotation. We support both client-certificate validation and token-based HEC as fallback.

2) Egress: we can constrain to 3 static regional IPs per region (US-West 2). Firewall rules: outbound TCP 443 to HEC cluster FQDN. We'll provide a CIDR set; if NovaBank requires a single IP, we can arrange a dedicated egress NAT for the Dedicated plan (requires pre-provisioning).

3) Scrubbing: two-layer approach recommended — (a) forwarder-side filter for guaranteed removal of high-risk fields, (b) runtime redaction rule as safety net. We can deliver a sample scrubbing YAML tailored to NovaBank's PI classification.

4) Trace hooks and stable header: we will emit x-nb-trace-id and x-nb-span-id in both request logs and span attributes. tracehook-spec.yaml includes the exact attribute names and an example payload for Jaeger/OTLP ingestion. Sampling is request-weighted; for SOC evidence we can enable deterministic 100% sampling for a short window (config flag).

5) Evidence bundle: we can create an auditor bundle with compressed logs (redacted per policy), trace samples (pcap-like JSON), a manifest, SHA256 checksums, and a PGP-signed receipt. SFTP/HTTPS delivery options available. See novabank-evidence-bundle-checklist.txt in attachments.

Open items for NovaBank: retention windows (logs / traces), any additional field deny-list, and preferred delivery method for the bundle.

Kim
Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks, Ethan/Kim — this is helpful. A couple clarifications before we sign off: 

- For the evidence bundle, SFTP is preferred (our compliance team requires in-transit assurances). Can you provide an SFTP host + user provisioning flow?
- Retention: we need logs 365 days, traces 90 days (redacted copies acceptable). Will the canary support 365d log retention for the test dataset?
- Token rotation: we will want a monthly HEC token rotation policy. If your forwarder rotates certs every 90 days, will that interfere with our monthly rotation?

Also please include a short mutual action plan / timeline we can share with auditors (who will expect an owner, dates, and artifact links). Our SOC window target remains week of Nov 29.

-Amal

Amal — agreed. Finalizing the mutual action plan below and next steps. I've attached the policy diff and evidence checklist again. Links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/novabank-obsv-handshake (workbook).

Mutual action plan (summary)
- Owner (Redwood): Kimberly Park (infra security) — contact kimberly_park@redwood.com
- Owner (NovaBank): Amal Singh (security engineering)
- Nov 17: Redwood provides SFTP host + user provisioning flow and updated CIDR egress list. (attachment: splunk-hec-mtls-notes.md)
- Nov 18–24: Canary deployment (customer-managed forwarder in NovaBank VPC to validate HEC ingestion, retention, and scrubbing). Redwood will enable deterministic 100% sampling for trace evidence during this window.

Notes / clarifications:
- Retention: we can map canary logs to a 365-day retention policy for the dataset we test; long-term retention for production will be configured in your Splunk index buckets (we will provide retention mapping guidance).
- Token rotation: monthly HEC token rotation is supported — if NovaBank rotates tokens monthly, Redwood will support an automated token exchange endpoint. Our mTLS cert rotation (90d) is independent; combining token-based auth plus client-cert provides layered control and will not block monthly rotation.

Attachments included: redwood-enclave-export-policy-v1.pdf, tracehook-spec.yaml, splunk-hec-mtls-notes.md, novabank-evidence-bundle-checklist.txt
